summary.done: Created index.html with canvas (800x480) and js/main.js with requestAnimationFrame game loop, dt capping, and stub update/render functions.
summary.decisions: Script loading order in HTML follows dependency chain: input -> camera -> entity -> sprites -> sfx -> game objects -> level -> collision -> game -> main
summary.tradeoffs: Capped dt at 0.05s to prevent physics explosion on tab switch. Used inline styles instead of external CSS for simplicity.

summary.done: Created input.js (keyboard tracking via keydown/keyup, arrow key scroll prevention) and camera.js (Camera class that follows Mario with 300px left offset, clamps to level bounds).
summary.decisions: Camera follows at 300px offset (Mario positioned left third of screen). Level-width based clamping instead of hardcoded max.
summary.tradeoffs: Camera only scrolls right (classic SMB behavior - no left scrolling past start). Simple global keys object instead of input queue.

1.3.name: Entity base class and sprite system

summary.done: Created entity.js (base Entity class with position, velocity, AABB collision, overlaps method), sprites.js (sprite sheet loader, drawSprite, getSprite helpers, fallback rendering), and generated assets/sprites.png (6x6 tile sheet with Mario, Goomba, Koopa, blocks, pipes, items, and background elements).
summary.tradeoffs: Generated sprite art programmatically via Python/PIL instead of hand-crafting PNG. Simple grid-based pixel art — functional but not perfect NES accuracy.
summary.decisions: Entity class uses simple AABB bounding. Sprite sheet is 16x16 tile grid. Fallback colored rectangles when sprites aren't loaded.
summary.lessons_learned: PIL sprite generation is faster than hand-editing PNG for functional pixel art.

summary.done: Created mario.js with full physics: gravity, acceleration/deceleration, variable-speed (walk/run), variable-height jumping, coyote time, jump buffering, death animation, grow/shrink states, walk animation frames.
summary.tradeoffs: Used coyote time and jump buffering for forgiving controls instead of strict input timing. Terminal velocity cap at 600px/s.
summary.decisions: Arrow keys + Z for jump, Shift for run. 100ms coyote + jump buffer window. Big Mario is 32px tall (2 tile rows).
States: small | big | invulnerable | dead. Invulnerability lasts 2s with blink effect. Mushroom grows Mario from 16 to 32px.
summary.tradeoffs: Combined 2.1 and 2.2 into a single file since they're tightly coupled. State machine uses string states: small, big, invulnerable, dead.
summary.done: Jumping and state machine already implemented in mario.js during task 2.1: variable-height jump, grow/shrink states, mushroom powerup, death animation, invulnerability blink.
summary.lessons_learned: Tasks 2.1 and 2.2 overlap heavily — physics and states are inseparable for Mario.
